measurements.tessy_access_2026_10_21: The ECDC site routes case-level surveillance microdata (TESSy, EpiPulse) through a data-access request process - not an anonymous channel; the anonymous surfaces publish aggregated country x disease x period data (Atlas viewer) and PDFs (weekly/monthly reports).
measurements.grain_2026_10_21: The Atlas data model is country (x age/gender) x disease x period surveillance panels - the same shape as WHO FluNet at coarser period resolution.

rejection_reason: Rejected as a task-shape mirror with an access blocker on top. (1) Mirror: the only binary prediction the publisher's anonymous surveillance data supports is 'will reported disease activity in country C exceed threshold T next period' - the exact formulation this bench already ships as who-flunet-activity-exceedance (ready, qualified as flunet-002 on 2026-10-20): same country-period grain, same activity-threshold target, same lead-time framing. ECDC's respiratory-virus products (Flu News Europe, ERVSS) are the same surveillance family FluNet draws from; a measles/legionellosis/other-disease version would be repeating last month's task on a different source, which the project's novelty rule names as not a discovery. (2) Access: case-level microdata sits behind the TESSy/EpiPulse data-access request process, and the anonymous Atlas is an interactive viewer without a documented bulk API (measured: the historical Output=json pattern returns the HTML shell), so even the mirrored task would need a browser-scraping construction the publisher has not offered an anonymous channel for. Both findings are recorded so a future tick does not re-open this publisher for the same task shape; a genuinely different ECDC product (e.g. a newly published event-level dataset with its own documented anonymous bulk channel) would be a new candidate, not a re-vetting of this one.
next_action: None for this record (terminal). Do not re-probe ECDC surveillance for activity-exceedance tasks; the flunet prior art settles them. If a future ECDC product publishes event-level data with an anonymous bulk channel (EpiPulse public exports, EU wastewater surveillance dashboards, etc.), open a fresh candidate rather than reopening this one.
